images.title: Kolam circle, wobbly and smooth
images.purpose: Show the chapter opener: a kolam doorstep pattern has a smooth round circle, while a circle drawn freehand wobbles and its ends do not meet.
images.composition: Two shapes side by side with wide space between them on a plain white background: the wobbly freehand circle on the left, the smooth circle on the right.
images.exact_structure: Left: one hand-drawn circle outline in grey #6B7280, visibly wobbly, with a small gap where its two ends fail to meet. Right: one perfectly round circle outline in teal #0072B2, with 4 small amber #E69F00 dots around it at top, bottom, left and right as a simple kolam touch. No doorstep, no people, no background. Exactly 2 circles and 4 dots.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a photograph, a crowd, a girl or a grandmother, or any scene background
images.takeaway: A hand cannot draw a perfectly round circle.
images.description: A wobbly grey freehand circle with a gap in it beside a smooth teal circle with 4 amber dots around it.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the circle that is not round and say how they could draw the other one.

image_decisions.why: The wobble against the smooth circle is the whole hook; one flat drawing carries it.
